description: Ability to interpret, validate, and provide expert input on AI- or automation-generated needs analyses, material, and business case recommendations.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: This element will now require the EC-02 to review, interpret, and validate automated analytical and needs-synthesis material generated by AI. The task shifts from raw preparation to higher-level critical review of pre-assembled material.
justification: Current expectations assume manual synthesis/preparation; future role requires ability to critically review AI-generated inputs, recognize limitations/gaps, and contextualize automated findings.

description: Knowledge of how AI generates, detects, or highlights statistical trends, including its potential blind spots, bias, or error types, to inform when expert override or supplementation is required.
historic work: Key Activities: Identifies statistical trends and developments.
change to work: Rather than relying solely on manual review/statistical output, trend and development identification will be supported by AI-driven scanning and synthesis tools. EC-02's role becomes assessing, interpreting, and prioritizing AI-generated trend findings.
justification: Recognizing when and how AI-mapped trends require additional expert insight or contextualization, and understanding how to tune or direct AI tools for improved output.

description: Skill in integrating AI-suggested feedback and recommendations with human subject matter expertise, including validation, contextualization, and clear communication for survey improvement.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: Suggesting feedback for improvements is now rooted in interpreting AI-synthesized analyses of collection and processing methods. EC-02 will validate, contextualize, and translate these insights for practical application.
justification: Ability to integrate automated recommendations with subject matter expertise for actionable feedback—knowing when AI output needs moderation, augmentation, or clarification for process improvement.

description: Ability to evaluate, critique, and where needed adjust AI-generated feasibility studies and impact assessments, bridging automated outputs with nuanced program realities.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.
change to work: Assessment and feasibility evaluation for new or modified programs will involve deep interaction with automated tools for initial synthesis and modeling of needs/scenarios. The work will emphasize the interpretation and adjustment of AI-drafted materials.
justification: Knowing how to assess the scope and technical foundation of AI-drafted feasibility studies and recommendations—spotting errors, oversights, or need for expert contextual correction.

development area: Synthesis of AI-driven and Expert Process Evaluation
description: Skill in balancing automated analysis results with expert knowledge to develop, communicate, and justify improvements to processes and systems.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.
change to work: Research/analysis activities are increasingly launched from AI/automation-flagged issues and results. The EC-02 will increasingly propose changes based on the synthesis of AI diagnosis, reserving manual evaluation for higher-order complexities.
justification: Ability to use, adapt, and supplement AI-detected process weaknesses or gaps, ensuring recommendations remain relevant and are not over-influenced by algorithmic limitations.

development area: Awareness of AI Data Sourcing and Reliability
description: Understanding the structure, coverage, and potential gaps in data sources as used by AI/automation for needs analysis, including methods to supplement or correct automated data synthesis.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability.
change to work: EC-02 must now also understand how AI systems interface with and pull from multiple data sources, including their constraints and curation for automated needs synthesis.
justification: Familiarity with the limits of AI-access to data assets, and what steps are needed to ensure reliability and comprehensiveness in automated synthesizing.

description: Ability to review, critique, and contextualize needs/trends identified by AI tools, and to intervene where additional data, nuance, or subject-matter assessment is required.
historic work: Key Activities: Identifies statistical trends and developments.
change to work: This task now starts with AI-generated outputs (trend lists, priority signals, benchmarks from external sources). The EC-02 evaluates, contextualizes, and refines these outputs for program decision-making.
justification: The skill gap is the move from direct/manual trend identification to expert validation/interpretation of AI-flagged needs and developments, including knowing when to trust, challenge, or augment automation outputs.

description: Skill in interrogating, validating, and integrating AI-generated findings when forming constructive feedback, proposals, and recommendations.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: Feedback and recommendations are increasingly based on synthesis of automated needs analysis and benchmarking, requiring the EC-02 to specialize in interpreting, qualifying, and supplementing automated needs assessments for survey/method change proposals.
justification: Gap arises because feedback is no longer based primarily on manual investigation/review but on automated, sometimes opaque AI analytics.

description: Understanding of how AI/automation operationalizes statistical theories and international benchmarks for need identification, to ensure oversight and improvement of tools used.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
change to work: The EC-02 must now also understand the interaction of AI-driven inputs and international best practices (e.g., automatically benchmarked recommendations), with a need to assess how statistical theory is operationalized and interpreted via automation.
justification: Need to supplement domain knowledge with literacy in how statistical/economic principles are instantiated in AI scanning and benchmarking tools.

description: Ability to dynamically integrate automated research/analysis outputs with expert-driven inquiry, especially when AI signals limitations in emerging/complex needs.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.
change to work: With automation doing initial scanning and proposal, EC-02's research and analysis must focus on higher-order review of AI-flagged issues, and on exploring emerging or complex scenarios that may not be covered by algorithms.
justification: Requires an ability to operate flexibly between automated insight and higher-level analytic thinking, with comfort in AI oversight and intervention.

description: Ability to assess quality, interpret, and escalate user needs and feedback synthesized by automated systems, with direct user engagement as needed for complex or high-priority issues.
historic work: Key Activities: Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
change to work: Provision of data/assistance is now mediated by an AI-driven consultation interface (e.g., user feedback synthesis, chatbots, summary dashboards). EC-02 is responsible for overseeing the quality of support, interpreting priority cases, and stepping in for user support in ambiguous or complex scenarios.
justification: Move from manual user support/data provision to oversight of AI-moderated communication, plus intervention in exception/priority cases.

description: Skill in validating and contextualizing AI-aggregated requirements, prioritizing them, and negotiating procedural adjustments or clarifications in partnership with automation outputs.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: Communication: Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.
change to work: Liaison now includes interpreting requirements identified via AI automation, validating accuracy and completeness, and negotiating contextual details with users and subject matter experts only for cases requiring expert input. Routine translation/negotiation of requirements is automated except for nuanced or complex cases.
justification: Skill needs shift from basic liaison and translation of requirements to critical validation of AI-generated specifications and skilled negotiation over ambiguities or priorities.

description: Knowledge of where human intervention is needed to supplement, confirm, or correct AI-synthesized needs and requirements based on deep contextual program understanding.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.
change to work: Contextual expertise is still vital, but its use refocuses on validating, clarifying, and supplementing needs assessments automatically surfaced by AI tools—ensuring human insight fills automation gaps and helps set priorities.
justification: Requires blending domain/contextual expertise with understanding of automated consultation systems and how/where they may misinterpret or overlook important contextual details.

development area: AI Output Quality and Compliance Validation
description: Ability to critically assess and refine AI-generated output objectives and accompanying quality measures for compliance with legal frameworks, organizational strategy, and user needs.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Analysis and preparation of analytical material now starts from AI/automation-generated objectives (drafts, proposed measures), which the EC-02 validates for compliance, completeness, and contextual appropriateness.
justification: Gap is between current manual drafting versus critical appraisal/validation role for AI-generated objectives and documentation.

development area: Strategic and Legal Adjudication in Automated Workflows
description: Ability to judge, escalate, and resolve strategic, legal, or ethical trade-offs surfaced by AI-driven proposal generation; ensure compliance and appropriateness in all analytical outputs.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: Feedback and recommendations for objectives focus on strategic and compliance issues detected in AI-generated material, moving staff up the value chain toward final approval and risk management.
justification: Now requires expert judgment regarding the sufficiency of automated drafts and an ability to escalate/adjust issues that are not resolved in automation.

development area: AI Process and Output Objective Literacy
description: Deepened understanding of how AI applications create, reference, and propose objectives, including where system limitations may affect legal/methodological compliance.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
change to work: Validation of outputs now includes strong emphasis on understanding how AI applications and automations assemble and draft output and quality objectives; must critically interrogate the technical underpinnings of automated objective-setting.
justification: Additional technical/system knowledge required to spot where AI-generated objectives may miss domain specifics or legal nuances.

development area: Final Concept Specification and AI Validation
description: Ability to critically evaluate AI-generated conceptual inputs, make theoretically/statistically informed selections, justify final specifications, and formally certify concepts for process use.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Preparation starts from AI pre-synthesized options for concepts. The EC-02 is responsible for detailed review, selection, refinement, and official sign-off, with increased focus on theoretical and statistical adequacy.
justification: Gap arises because staff will no longer be guided solely by precedent or collaboration; instead, they must fully understand, critique, and own the final conceptual specifications.

description: Skill in articulating and justifying conceptual choices, defending selections and rejections (including AI-suggested options), and documenting for downstream accountability.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities: Communication: Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.
change to work: Liaison now requires cross-functional communication to explain, defend, and document concept certification rationale, with an emphasis on reconciling AI-driven suggestions with organizational strategy/needs and formalizing final subject-matter positions.
justification: The shift to sole accountability requires strong skills in justifying and documenting conceptual choices, including explicit rationale for selecting/rejecting AI-proposed concepts.

description: Deep understanding of both underlying statistical/economic theory and the practical representation, error cases, or limitations in AI-driven concept synthesis.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
change to work: This knowledge is now paramount for assessing theoretical soundness of AI-generated concept proposals and ensuring that only viable, context-fitting, and standards-compliant concepts are certified.
justification: Staff must supplement traditional statistical/economic knowledge with literacy in how such theory/practice is represented or potentially misunderstood by AI tools.

development area: Certification and Documentation of Automated Data Audits
description: Skill in critically assessing, certifying, and documenting the adequacy, appropriateness, and limitations of data sources as surfaced by automated, hierarchy-driven evaluation routines.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: EC-02 reviews and certifies AI-aggregated data inventories/availability analyses, ensuring analytical work only proceeds with fully vetted and documented data sources.
justification: Current focus on manual analysis must evolve to quality control, critique, and documentation of automation-driven data source reviews.

development area: Automated Data Source Curation and Evaluation
description: Deep working knowledge of how automated (and center of expertise-supported) data sourcing operates, including legal, operational, and quality constraints, and methods for comprehensive evaluation and certification.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
change to work: Assessment of data validity now necessitates the evaluation of complex, automated audits and the ability to contextualize findings, flag shortcomings, or escalate for alternative acquisition agreements.
justification: Gap lies in requirement for heightened expertise in interpreting, challenging, and improving automated/AI-supported data inventories, and ensuring legal/operational compliance.

description: Skill in formally collaborating with specialized (center of expertise) teams, interpreting automated findings, and certifying/advocating for required system/process changes.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.
change to work: Proposals for changes to systems shift from manual research to interpretation and improvement of systematically automated search and assessment tools, in collaboration with data acquisition experts and for strategic process direction.
justification: Gap is the increased need for collaborative and documentation-focused process reengineering, and skill in working with specialized acquisition teams.

development area: Critical Review and Contextualization of AI-Generated Business Cases
description: Ability to identify deficiencies and articulate context, risks, and nuances in AI-prepared business case drafts. Capable of adjusting and defending proposals to satisfy oversight bodies and ensure actionability.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Preparation now starts with AI-generated business case sections; EC-02 must vet content, contextualize findings, spot gaps/risks/weaknesses, and contribute to strategic alignment of final materials.
justification: Gap exists between current manual authoring/reporting skills and future need to critically review, contextualize, and supplement complex, AI-produced documentation.

description: In-depth understanding of how AI-assembled business cases can miss, misrepresent or oversimplify contextual factors; ability to adjust, interpret, and justify scenarios and recommendations for an executive/governance audience.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
change to work: Now includes assessment of business case impact and appropriateness, by interpreting AI-assembled scenarios, risks, and resource estimates. EC-02 must ground these analyses in operational and contextual realities.
justification: Need for expertise in translating AI-identified impacts and assumptions into credible, defensible arguments for approval forums.

description: Ability to review, adapt, and provide analytic context to AI- and automation-generated design specifications, ensuring alignment with analytic objectives and stakeholder requirements.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Preparation and analytical work now entails interpreting AI-generated design documents/specifications, confirming they are analytically suitable, and flagging or adapting areas that require subject-matter-driven revision.
justification: Staff must move from document drafting to digital design product review, and must acquire the skills to diagnose/mend gaps in automated, machine-actionable outputs.

description: Skill in identifying, adapting, and documenting improvements or innovations within AI/automation-based design processes to better support analytic and operational objectives.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: Feedback and recommendations are now iterative responses to digital design elements and automated process outputs, requiring the EC-02 to participate in calibration and innovation rather than base-level construction.
justification: Where feedback was previously based on lived/manual design process experience, future feedback requires understanding and shaping automation and digital workflows.

development area: Digital Standards and Metadata Interoperability Literacy
description: Understanding of standard setting, machine-actionable metadata, and digital process simulation as they relate to analytic feasibility and program impact—skills to translate between automated outputs and subject matter deliverables.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.
change to work: Feasibility/impact is now determined through a combination of reviewing automated alignment to standards and digital simulation. EC-02 must assess whether automated designs produce fit-for-purpose analytic products.
justification: Gap is in understanding and translation of automated design outputs to real-world analytic/subject matter needs, and knowing how/when to intervene.

description: Ability to validate, troubleshoot, and refine standards-based automated process flows for coding, editing, imputation, validation, and estimation—from theoretical and statistical perspectives.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Preparation of analytical material relies on oversight and interpretation of automated analysis routines. EC-02 will review and adjust AI-driven codebooks, editing/imputation flows, and result pipelines, ensuring analytic soundness.
justification: EC-02 must supplement analytic skills with capacity to review, intervene in, and troubleshoot digital pipeline output.

description: Ability to appraise and propose changes or improvements to AI- or digital-pipeline-implemented survey and analytic routines, ensuring auditability, compliance, and analytic fit.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: Feedback/recommendation duties now focus on raising issues in automated methodologies, proposing pipeline or code upgrades, and ensuring compliance with new or evolving statistical standards.
justification: Staff will need fluency in both standards-based methodology (e.g., SDMX) and digital implementation to suggest meaningful enhancements.

description: Ability to understand, test, and refine (in partnership with technical experts) the alignment of AI-powered or automated digital pipelines with methodological/statistical best practices.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
change to work: This knowledge is now used to check for methodological and theoretical nuance that AI/automation may overlook, and to intervene when digital pipelines imply risks to analytic quality, repeatability, or compliance.
justification: Must possess sufficient literacy in both the underlying statistics/economics and in automated pipeline structure and operation.

development area: Interpretation and Communication of AI-Generated Analytics
description: Ability to assess, refine, and present AI-automated analytic outputs, making them meaningful and actionable for varied audiences and ensuring analytic communications maintain depth, clarity, and trust.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Now involves reviewing, validating, and tailoring AI-generated analyses, technical notes, and commentaries—focusing on contextualizing for audience, identifying deeper patterns, and adding nuance that automation misses.
justification: Current skills stress direct manual preparation; future requires synthesizing, interpreting, and communicating AI-produced analysis and technical material.

description: Competency in building meaningful stories, context, and actionable insight from modular, AI-discovered trends, and explicating them for diverse user needs.
historic work: Key Activities: Identifies statistical trends and developments.
change to work: AI and modular analytics surface trends and signals by default. The EC-02 will review, prioritize, and interpret these findings—linking them to narrative, social, and economic contexts, and identifying deeper stories or anomalies.
justification: Shift from trend discovery to value-added expert interpretation, requiring more narrative/cross-domain skill.

development area: Automated Results QA and Analytical Transparency
description: Ability to audit and explain the methodological/legal/definition-driven constraints of automated analysis results, ensuring accuracy and transparency in all analytic output.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.
change to work: Now emphasizes tracing, explaining, and refining AI/automation-generated results, with focus on constraints, limitations, and appropriate interpretation for users and management.
justification: Gap is the need for deeper communication, explanation, and analytic translation skills; manual process familiarity is replaced by transparency, QA, and sense-making in automated pipelines.

development area: Editorial Review & Narrative Tailoring of Automated Outputs
description: Ability to critically review, edit, and enhance AI-produced outputs, and to adapt detailed analytic content and explanations for diverse audiences (internal, technical, management, or external users).
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Involves interpreting and refining AI-generated drafts (write-ups, charts, maps, dashboards), and ensuring narrative is accessible and tailored for intended users.
justification: Staff must shift from technical preparation to expert editorial and context-providing role, which requires fluency in narrative creation, technical translation, and analytic communication.

development area: Technical Communication Gap Assessment in Automated Drafts
description: Skill to identify and bridge communication or explanation gaps in narratives and explanatory material generated by AI, ensuring correct and user-appropriate transmission of methods and results.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.
change to work: Focus changes from original drafting to assurance that AI-generated methodological explanations are clear, complete, and tailored to user comprehension needs.
justification: Greater emphasis on technical communication and ability to detect gaps/ambiguities in automated exposition.

description: Skill in reviewing machine-flagged outputs, exercising judgment on ambiguous anomalies, refining automated QA logic, and communicating judgment on critical issues.
historic work: Key Activities: Identifies statistical trends and developments.
change to work: Rather than discovering validation errors or trends by manual review, EC-02 now identifies which AI-flagged trends or anomalies represent genuine issues, require escalation, or are methodological artifacts.
justification: Shift is from primary detector to critical adjudicator and reviewer; requires interpretive skill and judgment, plus technical insight into AI validation logic.

description: Deep familiarity with automated validation routines, typical weaknesses/limitations, and ability to propose targeted analytic or workflow improvements for continuous QA improvement.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: Feedback and recommendations must now be grounded in experience with the kinds of failures, error patterns, or contextual anomalies routinely escalated out of automation.
justification: Demands experience with automated QA/validation pipelines and facility with their tuning and improvement.

development area: Advanced Editorial Oversight of AI-Generated Analytic Content
description: Skill to review, refine, and supplement LLM/AI-drafted analytic narratives and visualizations, ensuring messages are nuanced, accurate, and audience-appropriate.
historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Involves deep review, enhancement, and user adaptation of LLM/AI-generated explanatory material, with an emphasis on identifying where automated narratives or visualizations need contextual or substantive enrichment.
justification: Transition from primary author/producer of analytic text to expert reviewer, editor, and user-focused communicator.

development area: Critical Narrative and Conceptual Enhancement from AI Drafts
description: Skill in diagnosing and addressing conceptual errors and communication weaknesses in AI-driven explanatory outputs, ensuring clarity and value for all users.
historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.
change to work: Rather than authoring solely from scratch, the EC-02 ensures LLM-generated explanations accurately reflect concepts, clarify technical ideas, and remedy automated text's limitations for internal and external communication.
justification: Now needs the capacity to recognize and resolve AI-generated errors, vagueness, or absence of nuance.
